title: Query on a partitioned archive that touches every partition
prompt: Customer history summary for one calendar year, about 5 calls per second. Average 180 ms; for a partner account
about 6 s and 95,000 logical reads. Plan: Index Seek on IX_EventArchive_Customer with Actual Partition Count 32: the
seek on CustomerID runs in every partition, reads the customer's events of all eight years, and YEAR(e.EventTime) =
@Year is a residual predicate. The table is partitioned by quarter on EventTime and the index is aligned. The API
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.
EventArchive: 2.9B rows, partitioned by quarter on EventTime (RANGE RIGHT), 32 partitions from 2019 Q1 to 2026 Q4. IX_EventArchive_Customer (CustomerID, EventTime) is partition-aligned.
baseline_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS Events, MIN(e.EventTime) AS FirstEvent, MAX(e.EventTime) AS LastEvent

correct_families.description: A range on EventTime itself. The seek becomes CustomerID plus a range, and only the four partitions of that year are touched.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS Events, MIN(e.EventTime) AS FirstEvent, MAX(e.EventTime) AS LastEvent

traps.why: DATEFROMPARTS(@Year, 12, 31) is midnight at the start of 31 December. Every event later that day is lost.
example_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS Events, MIN(e.EventTime) AS FirstEvent, MAX(e.EventTime) AS LastEvent
AND e.EventTime BETWEEN DATEFROMPARTS(@Year, 1, 1) AND DATEFROMPARTS(@Year, 12, 31);

traps.why: An upper bound just before midnight drops events in the last fraction of the year on a datetime2(7) column.
example_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS Events, MIN(e.EventTime) AS FirstEvent, MAX(e.EventTime) AS LastEvent
AND e.EventTime <= DATEADD(millisecond, -3, CAST(DATEFROMPARTS(@Year + 1, 1, 1) AS datetime2(3)));

traps.why: A $PARTITION filter names partition numbers that move when the partition function is split or merged, and it still leaves YEAR() on the column.
example_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS Events, MIN(e.EventTime) AS FirstEvent, MAX(e.EventTime) AS LastEvent

min_improvement.basis: Four of 32 partitions, and one year of the customer's events instead of eight.
